definitions.explanation: The line of ancestry or family heritage passed down through generations. Refers to inherited family connections, traits, or social standing.

examples.japanese: {良|よ}い{血筋|ちすじ}の{家|いえ}に{生|う}まれた。
examples.english: Born into a family of good lineage.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}には{武士|ぶし}の{血筋|ちすじ}が{流|なが}れている。
examples.english: He has samurai blood running through his veins.

examples.japanese: {音楽|おんがく}の{才能|さいのう}は{血筋|ちすじ}もあるかもしれないが、{努力|どりょく}も{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: Musical talent may partly come from lineage, but effort is also important.

notes:
Composed of {血|ち} (blood) and {筋|すじ} (line/thread). Emphasizes the inherited nature of family connections, whether in terms of social status, physical traits, or talents. Can carry traditional or aristocratic connotations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {血筋|ちすじ}が{良|よ}い: of good lineage
- {血筋|ちすじ}を{引|ひ}く: to descend from, to carry the bloodline of
- {血筋|ちすじ}が{流|なが}れている: to have (someone's) blood running through one's veins
- {由緒|ゆいしょ}ある{血筋|ちすじ}: distinguished lineage

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {血統|けっとう}: pedigree / bloodline — more formal; often used for animals (e.g., racehorses) or royal lines
- {家系|かけい}: family line / genealogy — focuses on the documented family tree
- {家柄|いえがら}: family status / social standing — emphasizes the family's social position
- {血縁|けつえん}: blood relation — the biological relationship itself
